title: Improve quadratic Walsh-Hadamard agreement by 79,598,052 entries at rank 137 (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

A four-layer quadratic improves exact Walsh-Hadamard entry agreement over every parity interpolant on three consecutive overlap weights, at the same exact rational rank. Claim type: scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration.

```text
n = 16, exact rank = 137 in both constructions
best consecutive triple:  2,633,821,596 agreeing entries
new four-layer choice:    2,713,419,648 agreeing entries
gain:                        79,598,052 of 4,294,967,296 entries
```

For every n=4m with integer m>=4, use `P_m(t)=(-1)^m (2(t-m)^2-5)/3`, where t is the integer overlap. Its equality set is m-2,m-1,m+1,m+2. The proof gives exact rank `1+n+binom(n,2)`, the unique best consecutive triple, and a positive rational gain formula valid throughout that range. This compares two explicit polynomial families, not all low-rank matrices.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. It takes the equal-degree polynomial-comparison question in Jacob Alan Sussman / jacobalansussman's merged [#5817](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5817), Open next question 1. Credit Alman and Williams for classical consecutive-layer interpolation and monomial-rank background. The new step is the four-layer construction and its exact comparison; no predecessor result is audited. The original decoder card is explicitly changed to this low-rank side result. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

## Evidence

Before, the degree-two consecutive-layer family has best agreement 2,633,821,596 at n=16. After, the explicit rational factorization gives 2,713,419,648 at the same rank 137. `research/four-layer-quadratic-parity/PROOF.md` supplies the quantified proof; `verify.py` supplies a read-only exact check.

Local CPython 3.12.15 normal and optimized checks pass 125 dimensions n=16,20,...,512; ten exact count cases including two dense enumerations; 10,920 factorization entries; eight feature-minor cases; and 18 mutation, boundary and scope controls. The n=16 count uses exact layer multiplicities and an independent enumeration by row weight, not a dense replay of four billion entries.

From the worktree root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/four-layer-quadratic-parity/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/four-layer-quadratic-parity/verify.py

```

Any CPython 3.12 executable can replace that interpreter path. No external packages are required. Expected markers are `PASS_FOUR_LAYER_QUADRATIC_PARITY`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

Both registered commands also ran directly with identical generated package-hash receipts, taking 0.086 seconds each. The complete registered invocation took 0.402 seconds. These are verification durations. Metadata/pins and committed-byte/source-history checks pass. The official committed export passes integrity and declared-input coverage; both warning-strict modes pass in a read-only Git-free export with `PATH=/nonexistent`, reproduce the same receipts, and leave all seven exported files unchanged.

## Limitations

The claim is over the rationals, reals and complexes. It is not a global quadratic or rank-137 optimum. At n=40, a rank-one constant matrix agrees on more entries than this four-layer construction; the verifier explicitly checks that limitation. No per-row error control, operator norm guarantee, numerical stability, physical native realization, correction tariff or complete recursive invoice is supplied. No improved asymptotic non-rigidity exponent or multiplication theorem follows. The all-dimension statement rests on the written proof, not finite testing alone.

Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Lean and the selected supplier's cold replay were not run; no selected framework assumption is discharged. No local verification obligation was deferred solely to CI.

## Open next questions

- What is the best quadratic exact agreement, including constants? Classify the rational level sets at 1 and -1, then optimize their binomial mass. The present result does not supply a global extremal classification.
- Can a higher-degree nonconsecutive equality set improve a complete Walsh-Hadamard construction after row corrections and coefficient preparation? Start with one explicit factorization and a complete bill. The physical consumer remains missing.

## Related open work

- [#5982](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5982) proves spatial cut ranks and one-head travel floors for exact Walsh transforms. This contribution compares entry agreement of low-rank surrogate matrices; no shared numerical invariant is compared.
- [#5945](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5945) lowers a signed Hadamard connector with dirty scratch. Its exact query-call tariff differs from the rational matrix agreement count here; no same-instance number is compared.
- [#956](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/956) supplies an exact heterogeneous Gaussian/Walsh provider under its own RAM contract. The present polynomial surrogate provides no physical provider or tariff.

The merged #5817 is the question source. Its separate #5917 follow-up concerns acyclic Boolean-table tensor degree, not this polynomial model. Bounded main, merged/open PR and discussion searches found no matching four-layer comparison; those searches do not prove historical novelty.
